precepts.text: In as much as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. When we biting and devouring each other, when you be angry with your brother without a cause, you slandering him: you're not slandering us, you slandering Christ, because Christ put us in this position.
precepts.point: When the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them. So they knew: damn, this negro talking about us. Rightfully so. And they still wanted to lay hands on him, because the words was cut and deep, and they knew that Christ would take away their place.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

precepts.why:
In the parable the husbandmen, the Pharisees, beat the servants and killed the son. They knew who he was: “This is the heir; come, let us kill him.” To say that, they had to acknowledge the works of Christ and know this man is the Messiah, and they still rejected him.

Christ shows where that same hatred lands today: “Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.” If you do anything to one of these men, even give them a sip of water, you do it unto Christ.

Some of these black Hebrew Israelites right now may say, well, brother, we not talking about Yahawashi, we not talking about Christ; our anger is towards you, we slander you. No. When we are biting and devouring each other, when you are angry with your brother without a cause, when you slander and hate, you are not slandering us. You are slandering Christ, because Christ put us in this position.

The only difference is we can't do nothing about it. We are going to stay in the spirit and continue to do what God called us to do. Christ can do something about it. He can do a lot of things. That's why they call him the king of terrors, and the stone that falls on the wicked husbandmen “will grind him to powder.”

precepts.text: Many shall come from the east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, but the children of the kingdom, the wicked elders, shall be cast into outer darkness.
precepts.point: In Luke 20:16 they answered, God forbid: they would not give up their place.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
In the parable the husbandmen beat, killed and stoned the servants, the prophets, and then killed the son to seize his inheritance. Christ tells them who it is about: “The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.” The builders who rejected the stone are the elders. When he told the same parable in Luke, they said “God forbid”: they would kill Christ before they lost their place as the heirs and rulers.

Matthew 8 shows the same thing. “Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.” Those are the other husbandmen the vineyard is let out to, the people Ezra spoke of: “Your houses will I give to a people that shall come; which not having heard of me yet shall believe me”. That is us today.

“But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness”. The children of the kingdom are the builders, the wicked elders. It is written in numerous places that the sun shall go down upon them. “There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth”: they are going to die terrible deaths. And they are back again today.

So the kingdom is taken from the wicked rulers who killed the son, and given to those gathered from the east and the west who sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

precepts.text: I will bring thy seed from the east and gather thee from the west; bring my sons from far and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
precepts.point: In Luke 20:16 they answered, God forbid: they would not give up their place.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Christ said many would come “from the east and west” and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Isaiah shows who they are.

“Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth”. It is his seed, his sons and his daughters, brought back from the ends of the earth. That is going to us.

So the nation the kingdom is given to, the other husbandmen that render the Lord the fruits in their seasons, is not strangers. It is the seed of Jacob, gathered from the east, the west, the north and the south, the people “which not having heard of me yet shall believe me”, while the wicked elders, the children of the kingdom who rejected the stone, are cast out.

Whosoever falls on that stone shall be broken; but when Christ returns, on whomsoever it falls, it will grind him to powder.

precepts.text: The multitudes cried Hosanna to the son of David, blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, and the multitude said this is Jesus of Nazareth, the Messiah spoken of in the psalm.
precepts.point: God is the Lord which has showed us light. The light is the laws, and we are to bind the sacrifice with cords unto the horns of the altar and give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good and His mercy endures forever unto the children of the promise.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the Lord: we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord.” The multitudes said it to Christ as he came into Jerusalem: “Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.”

“And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this? And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.” The one that cometh in the name of the Lord in the psalm is Jesus of Nazareth, the Messiah spoken of here. This is the day which the Lord hath made.

precepts.text: Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass.
precepts.point: All this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet.

note.label: Matthew 21: The King Cometh Meek, and the Kingdom Taken Away

precepts.why:
Matthew says “All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet”, and Zechariah is that prophet: “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.”

Christ sent two disciples to fetch “an ass tied, and a colt with her”, and they set him thereon. He rode into Jerusalem lowly, on an ass and a colt, exactly as it was written, while the multitudes spread their garments and branches in the way and cried “Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord”.

The King the daughter of Zion was told to look for came to her just so, meek and sitting upon an ass. That is why the city was moved, asking “Who is this?”, and why Matthew counts it a fulfilment of the prophet.

precepts.text: Mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
precepts.point: He casts out them that sold and bought in the temple and overthrows the tables of the moneychangers, saying, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

note.label: Matthew 21: The King Cometh Meek, and the Kingdom Taken Away

precepts.why:
When Christ cast out them that sold and bought in the temple and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, he said, “It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.” Isaiah is where it is written: “for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.”

Isaiah speaks of the Most High bringing them to his holy mountain and making them “joyful in my house of prayer”, where their burnt offerings and sacrifices “shall be accepted upon mine altar”. The temple was given for prayer and for offerings that the Most High would accept, not for buying and selling.

So Christ was not acting on his own feelings. He held them to what was already written about his Father's house, and then the blind and the lame came to him in that same temple and he healed them.

precepts.text: The stone the builders rejected is become the head of the corner, therefore the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof, and the chief priests perceived he spake of them.
precepts.point: Christ is also a sanctuary, a place of refuge and comfort from the world, from crime, hatred, and murder, and he gives our people a purpose, which is what everybody is looking for. Simeon said the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and the "own" that received him not is the fall of the scribes, Sadducees, and chief priests.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Christ put the same psalm to the chief priests: “Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner”. Then the judgment: “The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.”

“And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.” The chief priests and Pharisees “perceived that he spake of them.” They were the builders who rejected the stone, so the kingdom is taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits.
